reuse.why: Builds on the tree's WeekendRule/applyWeekendRule/applyWeekendRuleToDay abstraction, and the new handler reuses recurConfigToRSchedule, applyWeekendRule and the shared skip predicate.

duplication.why: Non-business-day, holiday and skip logic each exist once; only getUpcomingDates re-states the daily-skip condition inline for its lookahead, and the lookahead/padding heuristics are written separately per caller.

placement.why: All date rules sit in shared/schedules.ts; server handlers and the budget template only call isSkippedWeekendOccurrence and applyWeekendRule.

scope.why: Covers the four steps (skip, range handler, holidays, MM-DD) with focused tests and the RecurConfig type, nothing unrelated.

maintainability.why: Clear small predicates make the rule easy to follow; the per-caller lookahead heuristics (take, padDays) and the early return inside applyWeekendRule for daily schedules are minor rough edges.

bypasses_abstraction.where: getUpcomingDates in server/schedules/app.ts recomputes `config.skipWeekend && config.frequency === 'daily'` instead of using the (unexported) isWeekendOccurrenceSkipped for its lookahead size

disguised_duplication.where: Only a one-line condition is repeated; no reshaped block copies.

abstraction_drift.where: WeekendRule gained frequency and holidays fields; applyWeekendRule gained a daily-skip early return; getUpcomingDates re-states the daily-skip condition inline. The additions reflect the real rule rather than caller-specific flags.
